title: rbac-v2: enforce KMS region-pinning and audit log propagation
author: Ava Patel
description: Motivation: Customers in regulated regions require that KMS keys and related ciphertext never cross region boundaries. We already have a soft audit for KMS region pinning but we have observed cases where RBAC v2 role mappings allowed cross-region key usage when fallbacks were in place. This PR tightens RBAC v2 enforcement to: 1) validate KMS key region against resource residency constraints at policy evaluation time, 2) reject requests that would implicitly route ciphertext to a different region unless an explicit cross-region-exemption label is present, and 3) ensure audit log events include KMS key region and matched policy id for downstream compliance pipelines. Summary of changes: - Add explicit region pinning check in rbac evaluator and short-circuit on mismatch with a clear 403 and audit event. - Surface KMS region in audit logging context and make it available to the audit-indexing pipeline. - Add a feature flag (rbac.v2.enforce_kms_region_pinning) with a rollout plan and a written migration note. - Add unit and integration tests for region mismatch and audit payload fields. - Update docs with examples and Linear/Jira links. Checklist: - [x] Add policy-level enforcement and unit tests - [x] Add audit payload fields and integration test - [x] Add feature flag and rollout plan - [x] Update docs and release notes - [x] Add changelog entry Backwards compatibility: Default behavior remains off until the feature flag is enabled for a customer. When enabled the policy evaluation will reject requests that violate region pinning rather than only emitting an audit. Rollout plan: start in audit-only mode for existing customers for 2 weeks, enable enforcement for new Dedicated/Private deployments only, then expand based on signals. Impact: This is a security-sensitive change that may cause 403s for workloads with misconfigured KMS keys; customers will receive audit entries prior to enforcement to remediate. See testing_summary and deployment_notes for more detail.
